subject: gmultmix model - Error in f * g : non-conformable arrays

messages.author: 5120c78945a3a2d1
messages.subject: gmultmix model - Error in f * g : non-conformable arrays
parts:
Hi everyone,
I'm new with this package and I get several error messages which
probably comes from the dimension of my covariates.
I have 9 surveys with 2 passes for each (so for the data I have a
n.site * (9*2) matrix). I have site covariates dshor and dudvlp (vary
at the site level) and yearlysite covariates peak_all, airt_all,
wind_all (vary at the survey level). I'm using the gmultmix model
because I have several seasons and I set the data with
unmarkedFrameGMM. The data looks good, as well as the dimensions for
the covariates (n.site*1 for the site cov and n.site*9 for the yearly
covariates).

Here what I have when I incorporate them
GMM<-gmultmix(~dshor+dudvlp+peak_all+airt_all+wind_all, ~1, ~1,
data=boat_umfGMM, mixture=c("NB"))
Error in model.frame.default(lamformula, siteCovs, na.action =
NULL) :
variable lengths differ (found for 'peak_all')

or
GMM<-gmultmix(~peak_all, ~1, ~1, data=boat_umfGMM, mixture=c("NB"))
Error in f * g : non-conformable arrays

I also have another question.
When I type summary(boat_umfGMM), I have Number of primary survey
periods: 9, which is normal (number of seasons) but I have Number of
secondary survey periods: 2. I was expected either 9 (9 repasses for
the all data) or 1 (for each survey there is one secondary sampling
period).

Thanks a lot

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] gmultmix model - Error in f * g : non-conformable arrays
parts:
Hi Sarah,

We should have better internal checks to make sure that the data dimensions are correct. Could you send some summaries of your objects so it is more apparent how they are formatted? Results from these (and perhaps other) commands would help:

summary(boat_umfGMM)
str(getY(boat_umfGMM))
str(siteCovs(boat_umfGMM))
str(boat_umfGMM@yearlySiteCovs)
str(obsCovs(boat_umfGMM))


Richard

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: gmultmix model - Error in f * g : non-conformable arrays
parts:
Hi Sarah,

I should have asked earlier -- what is your sampling design? Is it repeated removal sampling? If so, did you use

unmarkedFrameGMM(..., type="removal")

If it is, and you did, then I'm not sure what is wrong. You can email me your data if you'd like.

Richard
